pediatricPearls: Use pediatric dosing of medications or electrical therapy for a pediatric patient < 37 kg and as defined by the PEDIA Tape.
Pediatric hypotension is defined as: SBP < 70 + (age in years x 2) mmHg
Airway compromise / distress, singed facial or nasal hair, hoarseness / wheezing / stridor
Partial thickness 2° - blistering Full thickness 3° - painless and charred or leathery skin

pl1: Remove rings, bracelets, or other constricting items
If thermal burn: < 10% body surface area then cool down the wound with isotonic crystalloid o r sterile water
If thermal burn: After cooling cover the burn with a dry sheet or dressings
If chemical burn: Remove clothing or expose area, brush off any dry chemicals or powder, then flush area with large amount of water or isotonic crystalloid
Establish BSA, location(s), and type of burn
pl2: If airway burn: Nebulized Epinephrine for Respiratory Distress
pl4: Vascular access as appropriate for patient condition
2nd or 3rd degree burn area > 10% BSA then:
> Adult: Isotonic Crystalloid per Rule of 10s formula (Warmed, if readily accessible)
> Children > 14 years old: 2 mL LR x Kg x %TBSA with ½ infused in first 8 hours
> Children < 13 years old: 3 mL LR x Kg x % TBSA with ½ infused in first 8 hours
If cyanide toxicity – refer to Cyanide COG
pl5: Calcium Chloride for hydrofluoric acid burns with unstable vital signs, such as hypotension, tachy/bradycardia, ectopic beats, and/or ECG changes
